messages:
nora: Heads up 30z30 maintenance tonight 21:30-23:30 UTC. Objective: rolling NIC microcode + staggered GPU node reboots. We'll do 4 cohorts (2 racks each), 8m gap between cohorts, and a brief routing hold for each cohort swap. Expected: short-lived cold-cache for some inference requests while kv cache reseeds on backfill.

ash: Which pools are in-scope? Any dedicated hosts touched?

nora: Shared pools only unless a node shows host-affinity and is explicitly listed in the incident dashboard. We'll avoid dedicated pools. Affected labels: pool=shared-gpu-az30.

felix: Runbook sketch? I can take cohort B.

nora: Runbook TL;DR:
- 21:10 UTC: push manifests bump (HPA min+1) and notify oncall
- 21:20 UTC: deploy canary in eu-west1 (1 rack) to validate kv hit-rate + routing preference
- 21:30 UTC: cohort A cordon + drain non-critical workloads; run kvseed preheat; wait for kv hit-rate > 70% before drain completes
- 21:38 UTC onward: cohort B,C,D staggered with 8m gaps
- Routing: apply announce-suppression for 3m during TOR NIC swap, then re-announce. Smart-routing will prefer fallback regions for new sessions while announce is suppressed.

nora: kvseed example (controlplane):
```
./bin/kvseed --region az30 --cohort A --concurrency 6 --target-hit 0.75
kubectl cordon gpu-az30-01 && kubectl drain gpu-az30-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=120s
```

jun: If BGP hiccups, what's the fallback? Auto-fail to us-east/eu-west? Any risk of session split?

nora: Smart-routing treats announcements as hints; existing sessions persist where already connected. For new sessions, routing prefers us-east or eu-west if az30 withdraws. If error rate spikes >2% for 5m, we abort remaining cohorts and roll back manifests.

ash: Cost impact if we need on-demand GPUs for backfill? Budget?

felix: Quick calc: backfilling 2 racks for 1hr ~= $1.2k-$1.8k depending on instance type. Finance allocated an ops buffer; tag charges with "az30-nic-swap".

jun: Can we avoid excess autoscaling churn? Suggest temporarily raising pod disruption budget and HPA floor for latency-sensitive services.

nora: Agreed. We'll bump PDBs and set HPA min+1 for the window. I'll open PR now.

ops-bot: [scheduled] Maintenance ticket INF-2026-193 created. Window: 2026-03-24T21:30:00Z - 2026-03-24T23:30:00Z. Pager: infra oncall.

felix: I'll take cohort B and monitor kv hit-rate + p95. Will post metrics snapshot at each cohort boundary.

nora: Thanks. Checklist before 21:00 UTC:
- confirm PR merged (HPA/PDB)
- canary eu-west1 preheat validated (hit-rate >= 70%)
- cost tagging in billing pipeline configured
- ops-runbook updated with rollback conditions (p95 > 250ms OR error rate > 2% sustained for 5m)

nora: ping @oncall and @infra if anything weird shows up during the swaps. :loud_sound: Good luck, night ops.
